source.text:
But they're not wrong though, are they? Fridge automation shouldn't be directly accessible from the internet.

Directly sending monitoring/metrics? Maybe. Directly controllable? No! Absolutely not! At minimum, require a VPN tunnel to the fridges' network. They same should be true for anything that doesn't have to provide network services to the public.

Same goes for all IoT hardware (the S in IoT stands for security)

Is a vendor selling you a "smart" device, where the "smart" part happens only if you hook it up to the internet, and can be unilaterally changed at any time by the vendor because all the logic's on their end, not yours? Tell them to fuck off and put the "smart" on the device itself or you're not buying it, and while you're telling them that, tell them to fuck off with their subscription-based or subscription-alike business model, it's blatantly being done in the vendor's interest and not yours.

They may be morons, but the HYS crowd have entirely the right idea.
